population_one_line: ICU sepsis patients with positive BC, comparing satellite vs lab blood culture methods (Chinese single center)
ttp_reported: Median TCK (time from collection to instrument positive) 24.83h SBC vs 27.83h LBC (n=204 BC sets from 52 patients)
outcome_one_line: ICU LOS 15 vs 17 days; hospital LOS 18 vs 23.5 days; hospitalization cost compared; NO mortality data reported
notes: Method-comparison study. TTP reported as the primary metric. However, no mortality, persistent bacteremia, clinical failure, or relapse rates are reported anywhere — only LOS and cost. LOS alone does not satisfy inclusive 'clinical outcome' criterion. Confirms previous exclusion.

population_one_line: Patients with positive BC for coagulase-negative staphylococci other than S. epidermidis at a German tertiary care hospital (2011-2015)
ttp_reported: Median TTP 14h (likely infection), 16h (possible), 20h (contamination), p=0.01; cutpoints evaluated 16h and 36h with sens/spec
outcome_one_line: Overall mortality: 1 attributable death + 8 deaths from other causes (84.5% recovered); broken down by infection category in Table 1
notes: TTP used primarily as contamination-vs-infection discriminator, not as prognostic variable for mortality. But TTP summary statistics and cohort mortality rates ARE both reported in the same BSI population. Meets inclusive criterion. Mortality power is very limited (1 attributable death).

population_one_line: Adult Coccidioides immitis fungemia at Central California tertiary center over 10 years
ttp_reported: Time to culture positivity range 5-27 days (routine BC median 6 days range 5-7d; fungal-specific cultures longer)
outcome_one_line: Overall mortality 91% (10/11); 50% died within 7d, 80% within 30d of documented fungemia
notes: Small case series at n=11 (above the n<10 case-report threshold). Fungal BSI (fungemia), TTP and mortality both reported. Per-patient TTP and outcome in Table 2 allow descriptive cross-tabulation.

population_one_line: Adult septic shock patients at Korean tertiary ED registry (2014-2018); 1012 culture-positive incl. 803 blood
ttp_reported: Median TPP 9.5h overall (aerobic 10.2h, anaerobic 9.0h); survivors aerobe 9.6h vs nonsurvivors 9.4h; anaerobe 8.4 vs 8.4h; Spearman rho with SOFA -0.12 p<0.01
outcome_one_line: In-hospital mortality 17.1%; 90-day mortality 32.4% (CNSS 32.7% vs CPSS 32.2%, ns); TTP not associated with mortality but correlated with SOFA
notes: Large cohort with TTP summary statistics by survivor status and mortality reported. Authors explicitly state TTP not associated with mortality (descriptive medians only, no OR/HR). Under inclusive criteria, this clearly qualifies — descriptive TTP+outcome data extractable.

population_one_line: Adult E. coli BSI confirmed by BC at Hiroshima University Hospital, prospective ddPCR diagnostic validation study (2023-2024)
ttp_reported: Median TTP 9.1h (IQR 8.4-10.5); ddPCR+ 8.8h vs ddPCR- 10.7h p<0.001; septic shock 8.2h vs no-shock 9.3h p<0.001
outcome_one_line: 28-day mortality 9.9% overall (8/81); 47.1% in septic shock subgroup vs 0% in no-shock; septic shock 21%
notes: Primary aim is ddPCR diagnostic performance, but TTP and mortality reported on same E. coli BSI cohort with stratification by septic shock. No formal TTP-mortality regression but clearly extractable descriptive data showing shorter TTP in shock + higher mortality.

population_one_line: Adult Gram-negative bacteremia at 2 US community hospitals, pre/post MALDI-TOF + ASP implementation (2011 vs 2014)
ttp_reported: Mean time to culture positivity 22h pre vs 19h post (ns); pathogen ID time 32h vs 6.5h (p<0.001) after MALDI-TOF
outcome_one_line: In-hospital mortality 9.4% pre vs 4.9% post (p=0.07); 25% vs 2.1% mortality in those not on active therapy at TTP (p=0.006)
notes: ASP/MALDI-TOF intervention study explicitly listed as includable in guidance. TTP reported descriptively for the cohort; mortality also reported. No formal TTP-mortality regression, but contributes TTP distribution data on large GN bacteremia cohort.

population_one_line: Adult VRE bacteremia at single US academic medical center, pre/post Verigene BCID + ASP implementation (2010-2014)
ttp_reported: Median time from blood draw to organism ID 47.7h (CM) vs 18.2h (BCID); time to vanco resistance detection from culture positivity 50.1h vs 1.2h
outcome_one_line: In-hospital mortality 35.6% (CM) vs 26.1% (BCID), ns; 30-day readmission 31.0% vs 17.6%; post-culture LOS 14.6 vs 14.1d
notes: ASP/rapid diagnostic intervention. Reported 'time to organism ID' includes the conventional vs BCID assay turnaround, not purely biological TTP. CM-era values (47.7h, 50.1h) more closely reflect traditional culture timing. Mortality reported. Per guidance, intervention studies with TTP + mortality are includable.

population_one_line: Capnocytophaga spp. bacteremia in immunocompromised patients (mostly heme malignancy with neutropenia) at Chilean public hospital, 2014-2024
ttp_reported: Median TTP 49.6h (IQR 42.0-57.9); single species C. sputigena
notes: n=9 falls under the still-exclude wrong_design threshold of case report (n<10). Series labeled by authors as 'serie de casos'. Zero events also precludes useful contribution. Confirms previous exclusion.

population_one_line: Adult VRE bacteremia at US academic medical center, pre/post Verigene BC-GP rapid microarray implementation (2013-2016)
ttp_reported: Average time to VRE detection from BC collection 50.0h (pre) vs 24.2h (post); time to anti-VRE therapy 46.9h vs 30.6h
outcome_one_line: Hospital mortality 34.1% (pre) vs 20.0% (post), ns; hospital LOS 32 vs 20.5 days, ns
notes: ASP/rapid-diagnostic intervention. Reported 'time to VRE detection' reflects assay turnaround (Verigene shortens by ~25h) rather than pure biological TTP — pre-Verigene 50h includes biological TTP + conventional ID time. Mortality reported. Per guidance includable; contributes pre-intervention TTP distribution.

population_one_line: Adults with febrile UTI at 7 Dutch hospital EDs + 35 primary care; 131 (23%) bacteremic, prospective PCT validation study
ttp_reported: Mean TTP 11.6h (range 1.3-31.4) for n=25 E. coli BC at single center; linear correlation TTP with log PCT (R2=0.278, p=0.007)
outcome_one_line: No clinical outcome (mortality/clinical failure/persistent bacteremia/relapse) reported for the study cohort; background mortality cited from literature only
notes: Primary aim is PCT as predictor of bacteremia presence. TTP analyzed only against PCT biomarker, restricted to 25 E. coli BC at one site. No cohort mortality, clinical failure, or relapse data presented. Fails inclusive 'clinical outcome' criterion. Confirms previous exclusion.
